audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phases[].side read Akshan/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill while content win[] and packet.levelChart both read Skill/Akshan/Akshan/Akshan/Ekko/Ekko/Ekko — every row disagreed, and row 0 disagreed in the opposite direction. content mid also said level 6 'still favors him' while win[4] awards level 6 to Ekko.
audit.why: Two sources agree against the full layer, and the shape matches the kits: Avengerang out-chips Ekko from 850 through levels 2-5, and Chronobreak at 6 is what finally erases that chip.
audit.corrected: phases[0]=Skill, [1..3]=Akshan, [4..6]=Ekko, whys rewritten to match; content mid corrected to stop arguing the opposite of its own chart row.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes was the generic three-clause template and named level 3 as the turn; the real turn is level 6.
audit.why: Avengerang drops to 6s at rank 4 and his third-hit shield pays for each exit, so 3-5 is his; Chronobreak at 110s is the first thing that flips it.
audit.corrected: Spikes rewritten to 2-5 his chip / 6 Chronobreak / first item the string.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three ability facts were stated wrong or not at all. (a) content spikes[1] and mid both call Comeuppance global — it is 2500 range, and it stops on the first champion, MINION or structure hit, so a minion body-blocks it. (b) content early and whys[1] say his passive heals / sustains off minion last-hits — Riot's text grants a SHIELD, and only if the target was a champion. (c) Heroic Swing anchors to terrain and he is knocked off it by colliding with champions or terrain; nothing on the page said so.
audit.why: All three come straight from Riot's ability text and all three change how the reader plays the lane.
audit.corrected: Written into spikes[1], early, mid, whys[1], report[5], report[8], tradeGood, dosFull[0], dontsFull[2] and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ekko's E is a targeted teleport onto his next attack's target; Going Rogue's camouflage removes the target entirely, so the blink is not available while he is in it.
audit.why: This is the missingInteractions 'dash-denied' entry, and it is the reason the greedy blink loses here.
It is the field that must carry real numbers.
audit.corrected: Heroic Swing 18s at rank 1, Avengerang 9s down to 5s, Chronobreak 110s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8].t told the reader to 'Add anti-heal early into his sustain.'
audit.why: Akshan's kit has no healing — the passive grants a shield. Grievous Wounds buys nothing against a shield.
sources: enemyKit P flags: shield, no heal flag anywhere in the kit

audit.whatIsWrong: Lint: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim under 'Hold R for his real commitment', dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim under 'Fight in his wave at even HP', and breakdown.cooldowns had no number.
audit.corrected: All three replaced with bodies that answer their own titles.

edits.before: Comeuppance (R) is a long-range execute that can end your life from off-screen if you're caught low, and its global range means you're never fully safe even when you think you've escaped.
edits.after: Comeuppance (R) reaches 2500 and scales with your missing health, so a low bar dies from off-screen — but it stops on the first champion, minion or structure hit, so a minion in the line eats it.

edits.before: Akshan's Avengerang poke chips you down at low cost, and his passive lets him heal off minion last-hits so he doesn't even need to hit you to stay healthy in the trade — this makes early lane frustrating since you're the one taking consistent chip damage while he can disengage into camouflage after pushing. You mostly want to hold priority for jungle pathing and avoid greedy trades into his poke.
edits.after: Akshan's Avengerang chips you going out and coming back on a 9s cooldown, and every third hit on you shields him, so the trade he wins is wider than the bars show — early lane is frustrating because you eat the chip while he disengages into Going Rogue after pushing. Hold priority for jungle pathing, Q from 1075 rather than stepping into his 850, and avoid greedy trades into the poke.

edits.before: His level 6 Comeuppance is a genuine threat to anyone on your team sitting below its execute threshold, global range and all, so you need to respect kill potential even off-screen and play around vision to avoid feeding him easy picks. Your own Chronobreak doesn't match his utility for punishing overextension, so this window still favors him.
edits.after: Comeuppance reaches 2500 and scales with missing health, so anyone on your team sitting low dies off-screen unless a minion or a body blocks the line — play around vision and keep something between you. But 6 is your level, not his: Chronobreak lands at 110s and undoes the chip he spent the whole lane banking, which is the one thing his poke pattern cannot answer.

notes:
CHART: every full-layer phases[].side disagreed with the content win[] row above it (full read Akshan/Skill x6; content and packet both read Skill/Akshan/Akshan/Akshan/Ekko/Ekko/Ekko). I moved the full layer onto the content layer, so no win[N] edits were possible — before would equal after. Every side edit ships with its why rewritten, and ratings moved only on rows whose verdict moved.

FACTUAL CORRECTIONS, all from Riot's text: Comeuppance is 2500 range, not global, and it stops on the first champion, minion or structure hit — the page told the reader they were 'never fully safe', which is the opposite of playable advice. Akshan's passive grants a SHIELD (and only off champions), not the heal-off-minions the content early and whys[1] described — which is also why report[8]'s 'anti-heal early into his sustain' was buying a stat that does nothing here. Heroic Swing must anchor to terrain and he is knocked off it by colliding champions or terrain.

content mid also argued that level 6 'still favors him' while its own win[4] row says Ekko — corrected in the same pass.

REPORT SWEEP: two substantive rewrites only, report[5] and report[8]. report[3] still carries the old tradeGood/tradeBad strings verbatim and is now out of step with the rewritten trading fields — left alone to stay inside the two-entry report cap; flagging it here for the QA pass.

LEFT ALONE (templated, nothing Akshan-specific to ground them in): report[10], report[12], content late, wants.you[2] ('level 6-7 with items' is vague but not wrong).

UNVERIFIED, not written: whether Ekko's E can be cast onto a camouflaged Akshan at all (I wrote it as 'needs a target', which follows from Riot's own E text, and did not claim a hard denial); whether Ekko's Parallel Convergence anomaly knocks Akshan off Heroic Swing (Riot says colliding champions and terrain do — a zone is neither, so I did not claim it). | COHERENCE: 1 chart edit(s) withdrawn — they moved the row to the enemy while leaving the phase why describing the owner winning it.
